The 1949–50 season was '''[[Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]''''s [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|47th season]] in existence and the club's 18th consecutive season in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
During summer basque goalkeeper [[Juan Alonso (footballer, born 1927)|Juan Alonso]] arrived to the club from Ferrol<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1994/09/10/agenda/779148006_850215.html|title=Juanito Alonso|work=El País|date=9 September 1994|accessdate=1 July 2020}}</ref> along with him defender [[:es:Joaquín Navarro Perona|Joaquin Navarro]] was bought to Sabadell<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2002/11/06/mas_futbol/1036537207_850215.html|publisher=as.com|title=Navarro dies at 81 years old|language=Spanish|accessdate=1 July 2020|date=6 November 2002}}</ref> Shockingly the squad lost the [[1950 Copa del Generalísimo]] Semi-finals stage 3–5 against underdogs [[Real Valladolid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.es/archivo/fotos/el-real-valladolid-subcampeon-de-la-copa-del-generalisimo-4953326.html|title=Valladolid, Copa del Generalísimo Runners-Up|work=ABC|location=Spain|language=Spanish|accessdate=1 July 2020}}</ref> Michael Keeping managed the team towards the first spot on round 8 and remained here until round 20, then the squad collapsed for the final rounds closing on the 4th place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/blogs/ni-mas-ni-menos/2016/09/30/manuel-fernandez-pahino-la-imagen-de-un.html|title=Pahiño, The image of a Goalscorer|work=Marca|location=Spain|language=Spanish|date=30 September 2016|accessdate=26 July 2020}}</ref>
